notes:
Account summary: SableGrove builds a B2B customer success platform used by ~70 enterprise customers. They want to replace a hybrid of local rules + 3rd-party LLM for their in-product chat assistant. Primary goal: reliable live agent augmentation (co-pilot) and customer-facing chat. Timeline: POC on Hosted API (2 weeks) followed by evaluation of Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable cost.

Technical requirements: streaming required (client expects streaming rendering inside web chat), tool-calling for ticket creation / CRM lookup (via REST plug-ins), <1.5s first-token SLO for 90% of sessions (targeting p50 < 0.9s if possible), support 100-150 concurrent active user sessions during peak, average message length ~80 tokens. Also want predictable per-token economics and easy rollout to Dedicated for isolated workloads.

Security/compliance: they require SOC2 evidence, SSO (SAML) for staff, audit logs for model calls, and KMS integration for customer-secret wrap. A subset of EU customers will require data residency — likely need Private or Dedicated with EU region.

POC plan (agreed):
- Week 0: baseline data + sample traffic replay (they will provide anonymized chat transcripts)
- Week 1: Hosted API streaming POC with tool-calling hooks (SE will instrument latency metrics with Redwood tracing)
- Week 2: SLO run (sustained 2-hour load window mimicking peak, measure first-token and tail latencies) + cost run
- Outcome: if first-token SLO met and costs within band, commercial proposal for Dedicated (monthly commit + burst)

Commercial notes: pricing sensitivity — CFO asked for 12-month committed pricing scenarios vs. burst-on-demand. Key negotiation points: burst capacity pricing, sustained throughput discounts, and included observability retention.

Quotes from the call:
- "If we can't hit consistent <1.2s first token for the majority of sessions, we won't switch our agent UI over." — Head of Product (Anita Lopez)
- "Need to see real streaming behavior in our UI; payload shaping matters." — Lead Eng (Marcus Reed)

Open items / blockers:
- Need Redwood SOC2 + encryption-in-transit/out-of-rest docs (Drive link above).
- Confirm Dedicated burst pricing and any SLAs for first-token latency.
- Clarify regional routing and EU data residency path.

Suggested next actions for AE/SE:
- Run POC baseline by 2026-03-17; provide instrumentation guide for first-token measurement.
- Prepare Dedicated TCU pricing scenarios (monthly commit tiers) and a 90-day trial option for evaluation.

CRM flags: mid-market, price-sensitive, technical buying committee (lead eng + infra + head of product). Likely to go to procurement if POC passes.
